messages:
maria: Heads-up, jlee just reported a suspicious SSO verification email. Subject: "Action Required: Verify Redwood SSO". User clicked the link but says they didn't enter creds.

maria: Raw headers (copied):
```
From: security+notify@redwood-verify.com
To: jlee@redwood.com
Subject: Action Required: Verify Redwood SSO
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:12:03 -0700
Message-ID: <b827f3@redwood-verify.com>
Links: https://redwood-verify.com/verify?u=jlee
```

alex: Thanks. Did user enter password or SSO prompt? Any attachment?

jlee: I clicked the link accidentally. The page looked like our SSO page but the URL was wrong. I closed immediately, no creds typed, no attachments.

maria: Good — no creds. jlee says they signed in earlier today (normal).

tony: I forced a password reset and revoked active sessions for jlee. Also pushed an endpoint scan to their laptop (Intune + CrowdStrike).

alex: Uploaded the HTML to sandbox: https://sandbox.local/result/1776004321

alex: Sandbox verdict (snippet):
```
verdict: credential-harvest
malware: none
domain_age: 2 days
form_action: https://auth.redwood-verify.com/collect
c2: none
notes: page POSTs creds to external endpoint, no binary payload
```

phish-bot: automated-classification: phishing, high-confidence (score 0.92). IOC: redwood-verify.com (new registrar).

alex: Plan: 1) Block domain at email gateway + add DNS sinkhole, 2) Create SIEM rule for subject regex /Verify Redwood SSO/i, 3) Takedown request to registrar, 4) Check SSO and KMS audit logs for suspicious token activity.

maria: I checked KMS audit logs for the last 24h for any unusual key usage tied to jlee or this timestamp — nothing suspicious. Only normal admin service account rotations earlier this morning.

alex: Good. Also add a detection to the identity provider for any token exchanges initiated from the domain redwood-verify.com IP range.

tony: Endpoint scan returned: no malicious binaries, no persistence. Full AV clean, pending EDR posture report in ~20m.

jess: HR/Comms: will draft a short company-wide phishing advisory: explain incident, remind everyone not to enter creds, how to report, and that we forced a reset for the affected user. Include steps to check sessions and rotate passwords if they clicked and entered info.

maria: Follow-ups: alex -> takedown + SIEM rule + idp detection rule (assigned), tony -> final EDR report + confirm device clean, jess -> draft comms. I'll monitor for any similar reports and will post status in 24h. If no further hits, we close after 72h.

alex: Also recommending we require hardware MFA for admin-role accounts and add an alert for newly-registered domains that contain "redwood" within 48h of creation. Will open a short RFC for RBAC update + detection tuning.

maria: Sounds good. One more item: we should add this phishing template to our internal phishing-sim corpus so ppl get trained on this luring theme.

phish-bot: note: ticket created in SecOps tracker #SEC-2026-317.

maria: Thanks team. Closing loop in 24h with updates. :white_check_mark:
